survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD country note summarizes system-level indicators for Colombia using the latest available data from Education at a Glance 2025. It does not provide an analyst-facing microdata workflow (no student-level sampling frame, no replicate design details, and no explicit weight variables such as W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT). The note also does not describe plausible-value generation or item-level scaling procedures, because it reports descriptive and comparative statistics (e.g., attainment, unemployment by education level, wage gaps, enrolment/completion rates, and instructional time). For replication at the indicator level, users are directed to the Education at a Glance 2025 methodology/technical notes and the OECD indicator tables, which specify the underlying data sources and indicator construction.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a country note that reports descriptive education-system indicators (attainment, unemployment rates by education level, wage gaps, enrolment/completion, instructional time, and class size). It does not analyze student-level cognitive achievement scores from an ILSA assessment, so plausible values (PV-based achievement scaling) are not part of the reported analysis. Missing-data handling is therefore not applicable to the note’s presentation of indicator results, and the document does not specify any imputation/deletion strategy for microdata.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used indicator data for Colombia as presented in Education at a Glance 2025; the note does not define an analytic student-level subsample or inclusion/exclusion criteria.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD Education at a Glance 2025 country note for Colombia summarizes education-system characteristics using the latest available indicator data, with a thematic emphasis on tertiary education. It reports trends in educational attainment and labour-market outcomes (e.g., unemployment rates for 25–34 year-olds by attainment level, and wage gaps by upper secondary vs tertiary attainment), as well as participation and progression indicators (e.g., entry routes into tertiary, gender composition of entrants, bachelor completion rates at multiple timeframes, and dropout after the first year). It also provides system inputs related to schooling organisation (compulsory instruction time, school holiday duration, and average class size). The note is descriptive and does not implement student-level predictive modelling, plausible-value scaling, or an explicit survey-weighted estimation procedure within the text; readers are directed to the Education at a Glance 2025 tables and methodology/technical notes for indicator construction details.

It does not report an ML pipeline, target variables, model metrics, or an analytic student sample; therefore fields such as total_students, PV handling details, and main_findings are not applicable to the note’s content. The appropriate methodological details are instead provided via the referenced Education at a Glance 2025 indicator tables and the Sources, Methodologies and Technical Notes.
